```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
options(width = 120)
```

# Purpose

Each anatomical region is coded as a Yes/No severity variable from its regional
AIS (0-6). The cutoff used so far was AIS >= 3; this document gathers the
evidence on whether AIS >= 4 is a better definition of "severe". Only the
**training sample (2020-2023)** is used. The 2024-2025 validation sample is not
used here, because the cutoff was explored before this analysis and that sample
cannot be presented as independent evidence for the choice.

The evidence has three parts, always comparing the two definitions that can
actually be used (severe = AIS >= 3 and severe = AIS >= 4):

1. **Mortality in each definition**: how many patients each definition labels as
   severe, and how different their mortality is from that of the rest.
2. **Model comparison of >= 4 vs >= 3** with AIC, BIC and cross-validation.
3. **Effect of each definition by region**: adjusted odds ratios and the
   preferred cutoff region by region.

# 1. Data

The cohort is built with the preprocessing code of
`ultimate_validation_preprocessing.Rmd` (all code before the heading
"Preprocessed cohort" is executed).

```{r load-cohort}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

preprocessing_path <- file.path(
  "..", "ultimate_validation", "ultimate_validation_preprocessing.Rmd"
)
if (!file.exists(preprocessing_path)) {
  stop("Preprocessing document not found: ", preprocessing_path)
}
preprocessing_lines <- readLines(preprocessing_path, warn = FALSE)
cohort_end_line <- grep("^# Preprocessed cohort", preprocessing_lines)[1]
if (is.na(cohort_end_line)) {
  stop("The heading '# Preprocessed cohort' was not found.")
}

preprocessing_code_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
invisible(knitr::purl(
  text = preprocessing_lines[seq_len(cohort_end_line - 1L)],
  output = preprocessing_code_file,
  documentation = 0L,
  quiet = TRUE
))

preprocessing_env <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
# The preprocessing code opens a table in RStudio; it is not needed here.
preprocessing_env$View <- function(...) invisible(NULL)
invisible(capture.output(
  suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
    source(preprocessing_code_file, local = preprocessing_env, echo = FALSE)
  ))
))
retrascore_cohort <- preprocessing_env$retrascore_cohort
if (is.null(retrascore_cohort)) {
  stop("The preprocessing code did not create 'retrascore_cohort'.")
}
```

```{r setup-data}
outcome_variable <- "mortality_30d"
training_years <- 2020:2023

# The same 11 non-anatomical candidates and 6 anatomical regions used in the
# variable-selection analysis.
non_anatomical <- c(
  "age_category",
  "preinjury_antithrombotic",
  "prehospital_intubation",
  "high_risk_mechanism",
  "pupils",
  "gcs_le_8",
  "hemodynamic_failure",
  "respiratory_failure",
  "coagulopathy_24h",
  "mechanical_ventilation",
  "massive_hemorrhage"
)

regions_df <- data.frame(
  key = c(
    "head", "upper_extremity", "thorax", "abdomen", "lower_extremity", "external"
  ),
  label = c(
    "Head", "Upper extremity", "Thorax", "Abdomen",
    "Lower extremity (incl. pelvis)", "External"
  ),
  ais_var = c(
    "head_ais", "upper_extremity_ais", "thorax_ais", "abdomen_ais",
    "lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_ais", "external_ais"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

needed_variables <- c(
  "row_id", "trauma_year", outcome_variable, non_anatomical, regions_df$ais_var
)
if (!all(needed_variables %in% names(retrascore_cohort))) {
  stop(
    "Missing variables: ",
    paste(setdiff(needed_variables, names(retrascore_cohort)), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Derived severity variables for every region:
#   <key>_ge3, <key>_ge4 : Yes if regional AIS >= 3 (or >= 4), otherwise No
add_derived_columns <- function(data) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(regions_df))) {
    ais <- data[[regions_df$ais_var[i]]]
    for (cutoff in 3:4) {
      data[[paste0(regions_df$key[i], "_ge", cutoff)]] <- factor(
        ifelse(ais >= cutoff, "Yes", "No"),
        levels = c("No", "Yes")
      )
    }
  }
  data
}

# Complete cases for the outcome and all candidate predictors (same patients as
# in the variable-selection analysis), training period only.
cutoff_data <- retrascore_cohort[
  complete.cases(retrascore_cohort[, needed_variables, drop = FALSE]),
  needed_variables,
  drop = FALSE
]
cutoff_data <- add_derived_columns(droplevels(cutoff_data))
training_data <- cutoff_data[cutoff_data$trauma_year %in% training_years, , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(training_data) == 0L) {
  stop("The training sample is empty.")
}
y_training <- training_data[[outcome_variable]]

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Sample = "Training (2020-2023)",
    Patients = nrow(training_data),
    `Deaths within 30 days` = sum(y_training),
    `Mortality (%)` = round(100 * mean(y_training), 1),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Analysis sample (complete cases)"
)

fmt_p <- function(p) format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
```

# 2. Mortality by AIS level in each region

If AIS 4 is a better cutoff than AIS 3, mortality should rise clearly between 3
and 4 and not between 2 and 3. The table shows deaths / patients (30-day
mortality) at each AIS level; the figure shows the same with 95% Wilson
confidence intervals (levels with fewer than 10 patients are not drawn). Dotted
lines mark the two candidate cutoffs.

```{r mortality-by-level}
mortality_by_level <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
  ais <- training_data[[regions_df$ais_var[i]]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(0:6, function(level) {
    in_level <- ais == level
    n <- sum(in_level)
    d <- sum(y_training[in_level])
    ci <- if (n > 0L) {
      suppressWarnings(prop.test(d, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int)
    } else {
      c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    }
    data.frame(
      Region = regions_df$label[i],
      AIS = level,
      N = n,
      Deaths = d,
      Mortality = if (n > 0L) 100 * d / n else NA_real_,
      Lower = 100 * ci[1],
      Upper = 100 * ci[2],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))

mortality_wide <- sapply(regions_df$label, function(region_label) {
  rows <- mortality_by_level[mortality_by_level$Region == region_label, ]
  ifelse(
    rows$N == 0L,
    "-",
    sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", rows$Deaths, rows$N, rows$Mortality)
  )
})
mortality_wide <- data.frame(`Regional AIS` = 0:6, mortality_wide, check.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(
  mortality_wide,
  align = c("c", rep("r", nrow(regions_df))),
  caption = "30-day deaths / patients (mortality) by regional AIS level, training sample 2020-2023"
)
```

```{r mortality-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=6.5, fig.cap="30-day mortality by regional AIS level (training sample, same y axis in all panels). Dotted lines: candidate cutoffs >= 3 (between 2 and 3) and >= 4 (between 3 and 4)."}
# Same y axis in every panel so that regions can be compared directly.
plotted_levels <- mortality_by_level[mortality_by_level$N >= 10L, , drop = FALSE]
common_ylim <- c(0, max(plotted_levels$Upper, na.rm = TRUE))

old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (region_label in regions_df$label) {
  rows <- mortality_by_level[
    mortality_by_level$Region == region_label & mortality_by_level$N >= 10L, ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(rows) == 0L) {
    next
  }
  plot(
    rows$AIS, rows$Mortality,
    type = "b", pch = 19,
    xlim = c(0, 6), ylim = common_ylim,
    xlab = "Regional AIS", ylab = "30-day mortality (%)",
    main = region_label
  )
  segments(rows$AIS, rows$Lower, rows$AIS, rows$Upper)
  abline(v = c(2.5, 3.5), lty = 3, col = "grey50")
}
par(old_par)
```

The two definitions only differ in the patients with AIS 3 (severe under >= 3,
not severe under >= 4). The next table shows, for each region and definition,
how many patients are labelled as severe and the 30-day mortality of the severe
and non-severe groups. A good definition separates a high-mortality group from a
low-mortality group; what matters is how well each definition does this. The
comparison is crude (unadjusted).

```{r definition-table}
definition_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
  ais <- training_data[[regions_df$ais_var[i]]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(3, 4), function(cutoff) {
    severe <- ais >= cutoff
    y_severe <- y_training[severe]
    y_other <- y_training[!severe]
    fisher <- fisher.test(matrix(
      c(sum(y_severe), length(y_severe) - sum(y_severe),
        sum(y_other), length(y_other) - sum(y_other)),
      nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE
    ))
    data.frame(
      Region = regions_df$label[i],
      Definition = paste0("Severe = AIS >= ", cutoff),
      `Severe, n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", length(y_severe), 100 * mean(severe)),
      `Mortality, severe (%)` = 100 * mean(y_severe),
      `Mortality, not severe (%)` = 100 * mean(y_other),
      `Crude OR (95% CI)` = sprintf(
        "%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", fisher$estimate, fisher$conf.int[1], fisher$conf.int[2]
      ),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))

knitr::kable(
  definition_table,
  digits = 1,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Severe vs not severe under each definition: size of the severe group and 30-day mortality (training sample)"
)
```

# 3. Model comparison: severe = AIS >= 4 versus AIS >= 3

The same logistic model is fitted in the training sample with the 11
non-anatomical candidate predictors plus the six anatomical regions, **all coded
with the same cutoff**. The two models have the same number of parameters and
differ only in the cutoff, so they can be compared directly with:

* **AIC and BIC** (lower is better).
* **Repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation inside the training sample**
  (10 repeats, identical folds for both models): AUC (higher is better) and
  log-loss (lower is better), computed on the pooled out-of-fold predictions of
  each repeat.

```{r model-comparison}
spec_formulas <- list(
  ge3 = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, paste0(regions_df$key, "_ge3")), response = outcome_variable),
  ge4 = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, paste0(regions_df$key, "_ge4")), response = outcome_variable)
)
spec_labels <- c(ge3 = "Severe = AIS >= 3", ge4 = "Severe = AIS >= 4")

training_fits <- lapply(spec_formulas, function(model_formula) {
  glm(
    formula = model_formula,
    data = training_data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
  )
})
if (!all(vapply(training_fits, function(m) isTRUE(m$converged), logical(1)))) {
  stop("At least one logistic model did not converge.")
}

cv_folds <- 10L
cv_repeats <- 10L
cv_seed <- 20261109L

fast_auc <- function(predicted, observed) {
  n_events <- sum(observed == 1)
  n_non_events <- sum(observed == 0)
  (sum(rank(predicted)[observed == 1]) - n_events * (n_events + 1) / 2) /
    (n_events * n_non_events)
}

stratified_folds <- function(y, k, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  fold_id <- integer(length(y))
  for (class_value in unique(y)) {
    idx <- which(y == class_value)
    fold_id[idx] <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(idx)))
  }
  fold_id
}

# A predictor with a single value in a training fold cannot be estimated, so it
# is left out of that fold's model (rare categories only).
drop_constant_terms <- function(model_formula, data) {
  term_labels <- attr(terms(model_formula), "term.labels")
  has_variation <- vapply(term_labels, function(term_label) {
    values <- data[[term_label]]
    length(unique(values[!is.na(values)])) >= 2L
  }, logical(1))
  reformulate(term_labels[has_variation], response = outcome_variable)
}

# Out-of-fold predicted probabilities: one column per repeat. The folds depend
# only on the outcome and the seed, so they are identical for both models.
cv_oof_predictions <- function(model_formula, data, k, repeats, seed) {
  y <- data[[outcome_variable]]
  oof <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(data), ncol = repeats)
  for (r in seq_len(repeats)) {
    fold_id <- stratified_folds(y, k, seed + r)
    for (f in seq_len(k)) {
      in_training_fold <- fold_id != f
      fold_training_data <- data[in_training_fold, , drop = FALSE]
      fit <- suppressWarnings(glm(
        formula = drop_constant_terms(model_formula, fold_training_data),
        data = fold_training_data,
        family = binomial(link = "logit")
      ))
      oof[!in_training_fold, r] <- suppressWarnings(predict(
        fit, newdata = data[!in_training_fold, , drop = FALSE], type = "response"
      ))
    }
  }
  oof
}

oof_metrics <- function(oof, y) {
  clip <- function(p) pmin(pmax(p, 1e-12), 1 - 1e-12)
  data.frame(
    AUC = apply(oof, 2, fast_auc, observed = y),
    LogLoss = apply(oof, 2, function(p) -mean(y * log(clip(p)) + (1 - y) * log(1 - clip(p))))
  )
}

cv_oof <- lapply(spec_formulas, cv_oof_predictions,
  data = training_data, k = cv_folds, repeats = cv_repeats, seed = cv_seed
)
cv_metrics <- lapply(cv_oof, oof_metrics, y = y_training)

model_table <- data.frame(
  Model = unname(spec_labels),
  Parameters = vapply(training_fits, function(m) sum(!is.na(coef(m))), numeric(1)),
  AIC = round(vapply(training_fits, AIC, numeric(1)), 1),
  BIC = round(vapply(training_fits, BIC, numeric(1)), 1),
  `CV AUC` = round(vapply(cv_metrics, function(m) mean(m$AUC), numeric(1)), 4),
  `CV log-loss` = round(vapply(cv_metrics, function(m) mean(m$LogLoss), numeric(1)), 4),
  check.names = FALSE,
  row.names = NULL
)

knitr::kable(
  model_table,
  align = c("l", rep("r", 5)),
  caption = "Severe = AIS >= 3 versus AIS >= 4 (training sample, 2020-2023)"
)
```

The differences, with the sign defined so that **positive values favour AIS >= 4**:

```{r model-differences}
auc_difference_by_repeat <- cv_metrics$ge4$AUC - cv_metrics$ge3$AUC

differences_table <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c(
    "AIC (>= 3 minus >= 4)",
    "BIC (>= 3 minus >= 4)",
    "CV AUC (>= 4 minus >= 3): mean [range over repeats]",
    "CV log-loss (>= 3 minus >= 4)"
  ),
  Difference = c(
    sprintf("%.1f", AIC(training_fits$ge3) - AIC(training_fits$ge4)),
    sprintf("%.1f", BIC(training_fits$ge3) - BIC(training_fits$ge4)),
    sprintf(
      "%.4f [%.4f to %.4f]", mean(auc_difference_by_repeat),
      min(auc_difference_by_repeat), max(auc_difference_by_repeat)
    ),
    sprintf("%.4f", mean(cv_metrics$ge3$LogLoss) - mean(cv_metrics$ge4$LogLoss))
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  differences_table,
  align = c("l", "r"),
  caption = "Difference between the two cutoffs (positive = favours AIS >= 4)"
)
```

How to read it: for AIC and BIC, a difference larger than 10 is strong evidence
for the model with the lower value, and a difference below 2 means that the
models are practically equivalent. The range of the CV AUC difference only
reflects the randomness of the fold assignment, not sampling uncertainty.

The upper extremity and external regions have very few patients with AIS >= 4 (see
the table in Section 2), so their estimates are unstable.

# 4. Effect of each definition by region

## 4.1 Adjusted odds ratios

Adjusted odds ratios (Wald 95% CI) for being "severe" in each region under each
definition, from the two models of Section 3 (adjusted for all other predictors).

```{r adjusted-or}
odds_ratio_for <- function(model, term) {
  coefficients_matrix <- summary(model)$coefficients
  if (!term %in% rownames(coefficients_matrix)) {
    return("n/a")
  }
  estimate <- coefficients_matrix[term, "Estimate"]
  std_error <- coefficients_matrix[term, "Std. Error"]
  sprintf(
    "%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", exp(estimate),
    exp(estimate - 1.96 * std_error), exp(estimate + 1.96 * std_error)
  )
}

adjusted_or_table <- data.frame(
  Region = regions_df$label,
  `Severe = AIS >= 3` = vapply(regions_df$key, function(key) {
    odds_ratio_for(training_fits$ge3, paste0(key, "_ge3Yes"))
  }, character(1)),
  `Severe = AIS >= 4` = vapply(regions_df$key, function(key) {
    odds_ratio_for(training_fits$ge4, paste0(key, "_ge4Yes"))
  }, character(1)),
  check.names = FALSE,
  row.names = NULL
)

knitr::kable(
  adjusted_or_table,
  align = c("l", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Adjusted odds ratio of 30-day mortality for severe vs not severe in each region (training sample)"
)
```

## 4.2 Preferred cutoff region by region

Starting from the model with all regions at >= 4, one region at a time is
recoded to >= 3 (the other five stay at >= 4). The table shows the AIC of that
model and the difference with the model with all regions at >= 4. **Positive
differences favour >= 4 in that region**; differences between -2 and 2 are
treated as similar.

```{r region-aic}
region_aic <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(regions_df)), function(i) {
  region_terms <- paste0(regions_df$key, "_ge4")
  region_terms[i] <- paste0(regions_df$key[i], "_ge3")
  fit <- glm(
    formula = reformulate(c(non_anatomical, region_terms), response = outcome_variable),
    data = training_data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
  )
  difference <- AIC(fit) - AIC(training_fits$ge4)
  data.frame(
    Region = regions_df$label[i],
    `AIC, this region >= 3` = round(AIC(fit), 1),
    `AIC, all regions >= 4` = round(AIC(training_fits$ge4), 1),
    `Difference (>= 3 minus >= 4)` = round(difference, 1),
    `Preferred cutoff` = ifelse(difference > 2, ">= 4", ifelse(difference < -2, ">= 3", "similar")),
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

knitr::kable(
  region_aic,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "c"),
  caption = "Region-by-region comparison of >= 3 versus >= 4 (training sample)"
)
```

# 5. Limitations and suggested wording

* The cutoff of >= 4 was explored before this analysis. The evidence above comes
  from the training sample only and supports the choice, but it is not an
  independent confirmation. The validation sample (2024-2025) and the later
  registry exports (which include the same patients) cannot be used as such.
* A single cutoff for all regions is a simplification. Section 4.2 shows the
  preferred cutoff region by region; any region in which >= 3 is preferred should
  be reported and discussed.
* The longer version of this analysis (`cutoff_justification_completo.Rmd`) also
  explores cutoffs of >= 2 and >= 5, the stepwise models and the validation
  sample; its results should be consulted before writing the final text.

**Suggested wording** (adapt the bracketed parts to the results above):

*Methods.* "Regional injury severity was defined as AIS >= 4 (severe) versus
AIS <= 3. This definition was compared with AIS >= 3 using 30-day mortality in
the severe and non-severe groups, the Akaike and Bayesian information criteria,
and 10-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times in the training sample
(2020-2023). The cutoff was not confirmed in an independent sample."

*Results.* "The model with AIS >= 4 had lower AIC and BIC (difference [x] and
[y]) and higher cross-validated AUC ([a] vs [b]) than the model with AIS >= 3.
Mortality in the severe group was [x]% with AIS >= 4 versus [y]% with AIS >= 3
in [region(s)]. Region by region, AIS >= 4 was preferred in [regions], and AIS
>= 3 in [regions]."

*Limitations.* "The cutoff was explored in the same registry used for model
development and could not be confirmed in an independent sample; a single cutoff
for all regions is a simplification."
